title: Synthetic Snack Pops

all: Check every label for allergens before you start.
Let the pops sit out for a few minutes so they are not too hard.

byAge.1: For age 1, serve thin slices on a plate, without the stick.
byAge.2: Hand it over on the stick at the table.
byAge.3: Hand it over on the stick at the table.

steps.text: Line the tray with parchment. Cut the pears into 6 thick wedges and push a stick into each one.

toddler.1: Hand you the sticks one at a time.
toddler.3: Wash the pears, then line up the sticks on the tray.

say.1: Say it slowly: pear, pear, pear.

steps.text: Stir the yogurt and honey in the tall glass. Put 2 spoonfuls in the zip-top bag for later. Dip each wedge, let it drip and lay it on the tray. Freeze 30 minutes.
steps.ready: The coat feels dry to the touch.

photo.caption: Test caption: six coated wedges on a tray.

steps.text: Cut a small corner off the bag and draw stripes across each pop. Add 2 blueberry halves as eyes before the stripes set.

toddler.3: Draw the stripes with you, then place the eyes.

say.3: Stripe, stripe, stripe. Then count the eyes up to 12.

steps.tip: Go fast so the stripes stay neat.

photo.caption: Test caption: striped pops with two eyes each.

steps.text: Freeze for 2 hours. Take the pops out 5 minutes before serving.
steps.ready: The pop is solid, but a spoon can dent it.

safety.1: Slice it thin and serve it on a plate.
safety.2: Hand it over on the stick at the table.
safety.3: Hand it over on the stick at the table.

activity.1: Hide and seek. Hide a toy car under a cup and let them find it.
activity.2: Pillow fort. Build a small fort from two cushions and a blanket.
activity.3: Draw the pops. They draw the stripes and eyes with crayons.

tips: Chill the glass first so the yogurt stays thick.
storage: Keep in a sealed box in the freezer for up to 2 weeks.
madeIt: Share a photo of your Snack Pops and tag @tinysoho on Instagram.

review.countCheck: Test fixture. Not a real recipe.
